# COMMON YARD

## Project
- Building type: small urban shared apartment building.
- Residents: 18 young adults.
- Occupancy: one resident per private room.
- Occupied floors: Ground Floor, First Floor, Second Floor.
- Private rooms per floor: 6.
- Standard rooms: 16 at 20 m² net each, including private bathroom.
- Accessible rooms: 2 at 26 m² net each, including private bathroom; both on Ground Floor.
- Fixed entrance wording: COMMON YARD.
- Fixed controlled-threshold wording: Resident access.

## Surroundings

- West neighbour footprint: x = -12000 to -6000; y = 2000 to 34000; height 9600 mm.
- East neighbour footprint: x = 36000 to 48000; y = 2000 to 34000; height 9600 mm.
- North neighbour footprint: x = 0 to 30000; y = 44000 to 52000; height 6400 mm.
- East neighbour identity: three storeys, red-brown brick, four aligned window bays on the west elevation, pale concrete lintels, flat parapet roof.

## Accommodation and access
- Detailed room and occupancy records: 03-accommodation-and-use.en.md.
- Fixed enclosed room net area total: 522 m², comprising 372 m² private rooms and 150 m² shared and support rooms.
- Circulation, stairs, lift and wall areas: additional to the fixed room net area total.
- Shared and support rooms: all on Ground Floor.
- Visitor destinations: Entrance Lobby, Lounge, Guest WC, Courtyard.
- Resident-controlled destinations: private rooms, Shared Kitchen, Dining Room, Work Room, Laundry.
- Service Room access: operator.
- Accessible room entrance and bathroom entrance clear openings: 950 mm.

## Occupancy states

steps.userMessage:
COMMON YARD | Private rooms and shared living for young city residents

We are developing COMMON YARD for young adults who want manageable housing costs and a private room to return to. The building will house 18 residents in 18 single-occupancy rooms, each with its own bathroom: 16 rooms of 20 m² and two accessible rooms of 26 m². There are three occupied floors, with six rooms on each floor; both accessible rooms are on the ground floor. Establish the accommodation schedule first, then develop the building around it. The arrangement of rooms, shared spaces and courtyard is open.

The level site measures 30000 mm east–west by 36000 mm north–south, with the street on the south. Setbacks are 3000 mm east and west and 4000 mm north and south. Ground floor ±0.000 coincides with the south pavement; upper floors are +3.200 m and +6.400 m, the roof datum is +9.600 m and the height limit is +10.200 m. Enclosed rooms have 2800 mm clear height. Structural spans are at most 6000 mm. Two stairs and one lift occupy the western 6000 mm strip of the buildable envelope, with one stair at each end. Neighbouring buildings stand 6000 mm beyond the east and west boundaries and 8000 mm beyond the north boundary. The existing east neighbour has three storeys, a height of 9600 mm and four window bays on its site-facing elevation. Our material palette is a cast-in-place reinforced concrete frame, brick infill and aluminium window frames; concrete soffits remain exposed in Shared Kitchen, Dining Room and Lounge. All shared facilities are on the ground floor: Shared Kitchen, 24 m² with six cooking positions and 6000 mm of usable worktop; Dining Room, 36 m² with 18 seats; Lounge, 30 m² with 12 seats; Work Room, 18 m² with six desks; Laundry, 12 m² with three washers and three dryers; Entrance Lobby, 12 m²; Guest WC, 6 m²; and Service Room, 12 m². An open courtyard provides at least 60 m². Print "COMMON YARD" at the entrance and "Resident access" at the controlled residential thresholds.

Audience: the housing operator and prospective young residents, deciding whether the proposal offers affordable shared living with clear private boundaries.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the site, accommodation, access and material facts. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists every deliverable with its proportion, format and stage. 03-accommodation-and-use.en.md contains room records, capacities and the two occupancy states. site-envelope.png records boundaries, setbacks, neighbouring footprints and the core zone. section-datums.png records the permitted depth, height and floor datums. east-neighbour.png establishes the existing brick neighbour and its window rhythm. evening-neighbourhood.png provides the atmosphere of everyday street and courtyard life.

Deliverables:
1. One accommodation schedule, prepared first, listing every room's ID, name, net area, clear height, floor, floor datum and adjacency, plus circulation areas and floor totals
2. One site and massing sheet with the footprint, courtyard, neighbouring buildings, setbacks, core zone, north arrow and metric scale bar
3. Three furnished floor plans, one each for Ground Floor, First Floor and Second Floor, with room IDs, names, net areas, floor datums, structural grid, north arrows and metric scale bars
4. One private-room detail sheet with plans and sections of the 20 m² standard room and 26 m² accessible room, including bathrooms, 950 mm clear entrance openings and a 1500 mm turning circle in the accessible room and its bathroom
5. One shared-space detail sheet with a ground-floor plan and section through Shared Kitchen, Dining Room and Lounge, including the six cooking positions, worktop length, seating and exposed concrete soffit
6. One building section through the courtyard and a residential wing, with floor datums, clear heights, structural spans and roof build-up
7. One elevation sheet covering all four elevations, with opening positions, material boundaries and the existing east neighbour on the south street elevation
8. Two eye-level occupancy views: a weekday 14:00 interior view of Work Room with six residents working, and a 21:00 exterior view from the south pavement showing the entrance and evening use of Lounge
9. One resident and visitor circulation sheet with separate 14:00 and 21:00 ground-floor diagrams, controlled thresholds and a vertical route diagram connecting all three floors
10. One 10-second architectural video travelling from the south entrance through Lounge to the courtyard
11. One presentation document of at least eight pages, reusing the accommodation schedule, site and floor plans, room details, section, elevations, circulation diagrams and both occupancy views

Acceptance:
- The accommodation schedule, three floor plans, private-room detail sheet and presentation repeat the same room IDs, names and net areas from 03-accommodation-and-use.en.md: 18 rooms for 18 residents, six rooms per floor, including both 26 m² accessible rooms on Ground Floor. The schedule and floor plans also state each floor datum and account separately for circulation areas.
- The site and massing sheet, three floor plans and building section place the building within the 30000 mm by 36000 mm site and its 3000 mm side and 4000 mm front and rear setbacks. Show the western 6000 mm core strip with two stairs and one lift; dimension 2800 mm room clear heights, spans of at most 6000 mm and the datums ±0.000, +3.200 m, +6.400 m and +9.600 m in the section, with the +10.200 m height limit.
- The Ground Floor plan, private-room details and shared-space details show their scheduled areas and capacities: six cooking positions, 6000 mm of usable worktop, 18 dining seats, 12 lounge seats, six desks, three washers and three dryers. The private-room details dimension the accessible room's 950 mm clear entrance openings and 1500 mm turning circles; the site sheet and Ground Floor plan label the courtyard area at 60 m² or greater.
- The circulation sheet and two occupancy views follow the two states in 03-accommodation-and-use.en.md. At 14:00, six residents work, two rest in their rooms and ten are away; at 21:00, 12 residents dine and six residents join four visitors in Lounge. Trace visitors from Entrance Lobby to Lounge, Guest WC and Courtyard, and place Resident access thresholds before routes to private rooms, Shared Kitchen, Dining Room, Work Room and Laundry.
- The building section, shared-space details, elevation sheet, occupancy views and video depict the same three-storey building, with matching openings, courtyard edges and material boundaries. Identify cast-in-place reinforced concrete, brick infill and aluminium window frames on the section and elevations, and show the exposed concrete soffits in Shared Kitchen, Dining Room and Lounge. The street elevation and night view retain the east neighbour's three storeys and four window bays.
- Every drawing sheet and the presentation carry COMMON YARD as their title. The night exterior view shows COMMON YARD at the entrance; the floor plans and circulation sheet print Resident access at the controlled thresholds. The presentation contains at least eight pages and repeats the schedule's room areas and floor datums; the video lasts 10 seconds and follows the entrance–Lounge–courtyard route.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
